subject: putting custom text on a ggplot

messages.author: 634fcb21cb4f65a1
messages.subject: putting custom text on a ggplot
parts:
Hi Guys

I normally use annotate or geom_text to place some custom text/labels
on a ggplot. As far as I understand each time I do so both annotate
and geom_text requires me to explicitly put exact x,y coordinates
where I want the text to start. I am wondering rather than calculating
exact x,y coordinates can I use relative coordinates.

I ask so because it is difficult for me to know before hand how my
data will shape on the plot and which eaxt x,y coordinates should I
choose/use. If I could specify that I want the text to start at 80%
value of x and y axis then it will be helpful.

Thanks!
-Abhi

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: putting custom text on a ggplot
parts:
Hi,

the output of ggplot2 is grid graphics, so you can use any grid functions.
for example:

qplot(0:10, 0:10) + scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0))

gp <- grid.get("panel", grep = T)

downViewport(gp$vp)
grid.text("Text", x = 0.8, y = 0.8, hjust = 0, vjust = 0)
grid.points(0.8, 0.8)
upViewport(0)

maybe it is good idea to provide an easy way to annotate ggplot2 by
coordinate other than scale.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: putting custom text on a ggplot
parts:
You can also use +/- (Inf, Inf) as coordinates for the annotations (*),

last_plot() + annotate("text", x=Inf, y=Inf, hjust=2, vjust=2, label="text")

This approach is not always practical, unless you specifically aim for
the corners, with some possible fine-tuning of the justification.

HTH,

baptiste

(*) Now, it seems that (Inf - 5) for example won't follow the rules of
non-standard analysis and yield a distinct hyperreal.
